questions.stemHtml: The nut shown in the Illustration is used to produce
questions.solutionHtml:
Artificial bruise

The given picture shows marking nut

  • Artificial Bruises:
    • Some irritant substances, when applied to the skin produce injuries, which simulate bruises Juice of marking nut, Calotropis plumbago rose.
    • They are produced to make a false charge of assault.

questions.stemHtml: A man was involved in a scuffle and has some injuries on his body. The condition shown in the illustration occurs due to:
questions.solutionHtml:
Contusion

Hemorrhages in the soft tissues around the eyes and in the eyelids (spectacle hematoma; black eye), may be caused by:

  • Direct trauma as in contusion such as a punch in the eye,
  • Blunt impact to the forehead, the blood gravitating downwards over the supraorbital bridge,
  • Fracture of the floor of the anterior fossa of the skull. A bruise behind the ear may indicate a basal fracture, rather than a direct blow behind the ear.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 34th Edition, Page Number: 228 & 35th Edition, Page Number: 135, 137

questions.stemHtml: Some bodies were recovered from a bus that was involved in a road mishap. Identify the type of injury as shown in the illustration:-
questions.solutionHtml:
Brush burn
  • An abrasion caused by violent lateral (tangential) rubbing against a surface as in dragging over the ground is called brush burn or gravel rash.
  • It is a scraping injury over a large area. "Friction burn" (scuff or brush abrasion) is an extensive, superficial, reddened excoriated area without serous ooze or bleeding and with little or no linear mark.
  • It may occur due to tangential contact with a smooth surface or when the skin is covered by clothing.

questions.stemHtml: A child was rescued from a factory where he was working as a child laborer. He had multiple injuries, some were old and some were new. What is the age of the given bruise
questions.solutionHtml:
2 days
  • DETERMINATION OF THE AGE OF THE BRUISE
    • At first: Red(oxyhemoglobin)
    • Few hours to 3 days: Blue( deoxyhemoglobin)

questions.stem: A person was admitted with multiple injuries and a report of those injuries was made. Bruises are of less importance than abrasions because:

options.label: A
options.text: Their size may not correspond to the size of the weapon

options.label: B
options.text: They may become visible several hours or even one to two days after the injury

options.label: D
options.text: Both bruise and abrasion are equally important

questions.solutionHtml:
Both of the above
  • Bruises are of less value than abrasions because:
  • Option A: Their size may not correspond to the size of the weapon.
  • Option B: They may become visible several hours or even one to two days after the injury.
    • They may appear away from the actual site of injury.
    • They do not indicate the direction in which the force was applied.

questions.stemHtml: A person was taken to the accident wing after a road mishap. Identify the type of injury
questions.solutionHtml:
Shearing laceration
  • Avulsion (shearing laceration) :
    • An avulsion is a laceration produced by sufficient force (shearing force) delivered at an acute angle to detach (tear off) a portion of a traumatized surface or viscus from its attachments.
    • The shearing and grinding force by weight, such as a lorry wheel passing over a limb may produce separation of the skin from the underlying tissues (avulsion) over a relatively large area. This is called "flying"
